A motion to refer is a parliamentary procedure used to send a pending main motion to a smaller group, such as a committee or staff, for further investigation, research, or refinement. It allows the assembly to delay a final vote to gather more information or handle complex details. 

Passing the motion to refer H.Res.1100 to the House Ethics Committee effectively delayed or halted the immediate effort to release records related to sexual harassment allegations against House members. 357 congressmen voted to delay or block the efforts of Representative Mace. Why? Slush Fund!

Since 1997, over 18 million has been paid out, with critics arguing the process shielded abusers and lacked transparency.
